history.heading: Ancient land
paragraphs: The land between the Mediterranean and the Jordan River has been inhabited since prehistoric times; Jericho is one of the oldest towns in the world. In the Iron Age, the kingdoms of Israel and Judah emerged. Jerusalem became the capital of the Jewish kingdom, and the First Temple was built there. The Hebrew Bible was largely composed in this period and after.

The region was conquered by Assyrians, Babylonians, who destroyed the First Temple in 587 BCE, Persians, Greeks and Romans. After Jewish revolts against Rome, the Second Temple was destroyed in 70 CE, and many Jews were dispersed, forming a diaspora. Christianity arose in the region in the 1st century.

history.heading: Empires and Zionism
paragraphs: The land was ruled by Byzantines, Arab caliphates, from the 7th century, Crusaders, Mamluks and, from 1517, the Ottoman Empire. Its population became mostly Arab and Muslim, with Christian and Jewish communities.

In the late 19th century the Zionist movement, founded by Theodor Herzl in response to antisemitism in Europe, sought a Jewish homeland, and Jewish immigration increased. After the First World War Britain governed Palestine under a League of Nations mandate; the 1917 Balfour Declaration supported a Jewish national home. Tensions between Jewish and Arab communities grew.

history.heading: Founding of Israel
paragraphs: After the Holocaust, in which six million Jews were murdered, the UN proposed partitioning Palestine into Jewish and Arab states in 1947. Israel declared independence on 14 May 1948. In the war that followed with Arab states, Israel expanded its territory, and about 700,000 Palestinians fled or were expelled, an event Palestinians call the Nakba (catastrophe).

Israel fought further wars in 1956, 1967 and 1973. In the 1967 Six-Day War it captured the West Bank, East Jerusalem, Gaza, the Sinai and the Golan Heights. Israel made peace with Egypt in 1979 and Jordan in 1994, and normalised relations with several Arab states in the 2020 Abraham Accords.

history.heading: Conflict with the Palestinians
paragraphs: The 1993 Oslo Accords created the Palestinian Authority, but peace talks failed, and two Palestinian uprisings (intifadas) occurred. Israel withdrew from Gaza in 2005; Hamas took control there in 2007.

On 7 October 2023, Hamas-led militants attacked southern Israel, killing about 1,200 people and taking around 250 hostages. Israel's ensuing war in Gaza killed tens of thousands of Palestinians, caused a humanitarian catastrophe and widespread destruction, and led to international legal proceedings. Conflicts also involved Hezbollah in Lebanon and Iran. A ceasefire took effect in October 2025.

culture.heading: Peoples and languages
paragraphs: Hebrew, revived as a spoken language in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, is the official language; Arabic has special status. About three-quarters of citizens are Jewish, from diverse backgrounds including Ashkenazi, Sephardi and Mizrahi, Ethiopian and Russian-speaking communities, and about a fifth are Arab citizens, mostly Muslim, with Christian and Druze minorities.
Jerusalem is sacred to Judaism, Christianity and Islam, with sites such as the Western Wall, the Church of the Holy Sepulchre and the Al-Aqsa Mosque.

culture.heading: Culture and daily life
paragraphs: Israeli culture blends influences from Jewish communities around the world and the Middle East. Literature includes Nobel laureate S. Y. Agnon and authors such as Amos Oz and David Grossman. Israeli television series have found international audiences.
Food includes falafel, hummus, shakshuka and sabich. The Sabbath, from Friday evening to Saturday evening, shapes the weekly rhythm.

politics.heading: Parliamentary democracy
paragraphs: Israel is a parliamentary democracy without a written constitution, relying on Basic Laws. The 120-member Knesset is elected by proportional representation, producing coalition governments. The prime minister leads the government, and the president has a largely ceremonial role. Benjamin Netanyahu has been the longest-serving prime minister.

A 2023 government plan to curb the power of the judiciary provoked some of the largest protests in the country's history. Politics is deeply divided over the judiciary, religion and state, and the Palestinian conflict.

politics.heading: Occupation and international relations
paragraphs: Israel controls the West Bank, where hundreds of thousands of Israelis live in settlements considered illegal under international law by most countries; Israel disputes this. It annexed East Jerusalem and the Golan Heights, moves not recognised by most of the world. The United States is its closest ally and a major provider of military aid.

economy.heading: The start-up nation
paragraphs: Israel has a high-income, technologically advanced economy and is known as the "start-up nation", with one of the highest concentrations of tech companies and research spending in the world. Key sectors include software, cybersecurity, semiconductors, medical technology, pharmaceuticals, defence and cut diamonds. Offshore natural gas fields have made it an energy exporter.
The currency is the new shekel. Challenges include a high cost of living, housing prices, and the economic costs of war.
